messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Inference-api: 5xx rate > 8% over 5m (service=inference-api, region=us-west-2). Pager triggered.
Maya (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm on it. Paging Ajay and Priya.
Ajay: I'm pulling logs now. getting a lot of `connection reset by peer` and 503 from model-backend. Starting a quick timeline.
Priya (Runtime): Not seeing recent deploys to model-backend in the last 2h. Any config changes? Could be autoscaler or network.
Jordan (ops): Gate metrics show burst in concurrent connections starting 06:12 UTC. Autoscaler didn't kick until 06:16.
Maya (oncall): Customer-impact report: several customers reported failed generations, elevated error pages. CSM Liz is monitoring for any P0 customers.
Liz (CSM): Confirmed two enterprise customers hit errors and raised tickets. Sending enterprise-level notes to them; need ETA.
Ajay: Quick log query (Datadog):
```
logs("service:inference-api AND status:5xx").rollup("count").by("http.target").last(10m)
```
Shows the traffic concentrated on /v1/generate route and increased latencies to model-backend.
Maya (oncall): Hypotheses:
- H1: model-backend overloaded (CPU/GRPC errors)
- H2: network flapping in us-west-2 (LB->backend)
- H3: log sampling/aggregation hiding crucial traces
Priya (Runtime): Running `kubectl top pods -n inference` now; some model-backend pods at 95% CPU. Could be CPU saturation + garbage collection pauses.
Ajay: Also noticing many logs missing request bodies — the request-redaction rule rolled out yesterday is stripping payloads for non-prod but matched prod by mistake.
Maya (oncall): That's our observability gap. Need to temporarily increase log sampling/retention and disable the overzealous redaction for prod.
Jordan (ops): I can flip sampling for 10 minutes. Command:
```
redwood-monitoring config set log_sampling=100 --service=inference-api --env=prod
```
will increase sample rate. Approving now.
ops-bot: Executed: `redwood-monitoring config set ...` — change queued, rollout started (config-id: cfg_87b14).
Ajay: New logs show full request headers now. Seeing repeated `grpc: received message larger than max` errors from model-backend at 06:15:23.
Priya (Runtime): That points to a mismatch in max message size after a new model shard landed. Rolling back the latest model-backend release to previous commit `a1c3f2` as mitigation.
Maya (oncall): Do that, Priya. Also open a canary route to fallback model for critical customers.
Priya (Runtime): Rollback initiated.
ops-bot: Deploy rollback started: deployment/model-backend -> a1c3f2
Jordan (ops): While rollback is happening, scaling up pool by +4 pods to absorb burst.
Ajay: Building timeline (concise):
- 06:08: config change: redaction rule deployed (sampling adjusted)
- 06:12: traffic spike to /v1/generate
- 06:15: first gRPC `message too large` errors
- 06:16: autoscaler delayed, pods saturated
- 06:18: rollback triggered
Maya (oncall): Good. Make sure we capture correlating traces — request ids for impacted requests: `req-9a7c`, `req-b3f2`, `req-c1d4`. Add to incident doc.
Ajay: Saving extracted logs to s3: `s3://redwood-incidents/1791004321/` (presigned link sent to SRE triage).
Liz (CSM): Notifying impacted customers: will send an update in 15 minutes once rollback confirms.
Priya (Runtime): Rollback complete. Model-backend reports healthy, errors dropping to baseline.
ops-bot: Canary routing applied for critical customers -> fallback-model
Maya (oncall): Verification: monitoring shows 5xx rate back to 0.7% at 06:28.
Ajay: Post-mortem notes (in-thread): Observability gaps:
- Redaction rule accidentally matched prod -> lost request bodies for first 10 minutes of incident
- Log sampling set too low for error debug (we had 1% sampling)
- Dashboards didn't show gRPC message size metric by default
Actions (owner):
- Ajay: Add `grpc.msg_size` to default inference-api dashboard and create alert (due EOD)
- Priya: Add guard in model-backend deploys to validate `max_message_size` with schema (PR opened)
- Jordan: Make sampling change reversible via runbook and add a one-click "high-fidelity logs" toggle in Console
- Maya: Draft incident timeline and customer postmortem
Maya (oncall): Anything else? If not, I'll close the incident and schedule a follow-up RCA with owners listed.
Liz (CSM): Please cc me on postmortem so I can follow up with customers.
Maya (oncall): Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
